paper_metadata.title: Quantum computational finance: Monte Carlo pricing of financial derivatives

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum Monte Carlo pricing of a European call option using amplitude estimation, with a discretized Gaussian Brownian-motion distribution and a reversible payoff circuit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with amplitude estimation for mean estimation / phase estimation

hyperparameters.n: number of qubits used to discretize the Brownian-motion distribution
hyperparameters.xmax: O(sqrt(T)) cutoff for truncating the Gaussian support
hyperparameters.delta: failure probability for boosted amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare a discretized Gaussian state over 2^n grid points for Brownian motion WT using Grover-Rudolph state preparation; encode the call payoff into an ancilla rotation via a reversible payoff circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Pi = e^{-rT} E_Q[max(0, S0*exp(sigma*WT + (r - sigma^2/2)T) - K)]

problem_instance.description: European call option under the Black-Scholes-Merton model; numerical illustration uses S0 = 100, K = 50, r = 0.05, sigma = 0.2, T = 1.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic BSM model with Gaussian Brownian motion; discretized support truncated to [-xmax, xmax].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate Gaussian support, discretize into 2^n points, normalize probabilities, approximate payoff function with n-bit reversible arithmetic.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Classical numerical simulations compare quantum phase-estimation error scaling against classical Monte Carlo; confidence > 99.5% achieved by D ≈ 24 independent phase-estimation runs.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: n + 1 for state preparation and ancilla; m additional qubits for phase estimation register in the full algorithm
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: O(n) for state preparation and payoff circuit; phase estimation uses controlled applications of Q up to t times

hardware.framework: Strawberry Fields / ProjectQ (mentioned as possible simulation tools); single-qubit phase estimation used for numerics

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute analytical Black-Scholes price for benchmarking; discretize Gaussian distribution; compute payoff values on grid.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated phase theta back to price via Pi = S0*(1 - cos(theta/2))/2? (paper uses theta = 2 arccos(1 - 2Pi/S0)); estimate error |Pi_hat - Pi|.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Error scaling fit reported as approximately k^{-0.982} for quantum phase estimation

results.value: m additional qubits for phase estimation register

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming efficient state preparation of the risk-neutral distribution and efficient reversible payoff computation; for additive error epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: Speedup is in sample/oracle-query complexity; total runtime also includes polylogarithmic factors and discretization error O(2^-n).

speedup_claims.conditions: single-qubit phase-estimation surrogate simulation with D ≈ 24 independent runs and S0=100, K=50, r=0.05, sigma=0.2, T=1
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a surrogate numerical demonstration, not a full fault-tolerant implementation; fitted quantum exponent was -0.982 versus classical -0.5.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(lambda/epsilon) up to polylogarithmic factors for amplitude estimation-based mean estimation
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(lambda^2/epsilon^2) samples for classical Monte Carlo

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum Monte Carlo pricing of an arithmetic Asian call option using amplitude estimation, with multiple discretized Brownian-motion time slices and a sequential reversible averaging circuit.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo for Asian option pricing with amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare L copies of a discretized Gaussian state for Brownian increments with variance Delta_t; compute the arithmetic or geometric average stock price along the path in a reversible register; rotate an ancilla according to the Asian payoff.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate EQ[max(0, A_T - K)] where A_T is the arithmetic mean of stock prices over L time points.

problem_instance.description: Asian call option under the Black-Scholes-Merton model; arithmetic averaging is the Monte Carlo-relevant case, geometric averaging is analytically solvable.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic BSM path simulation with equally spaced monitoring times t1 < ... < tL and Delta_t = T/L.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize each Brownian increment distribution; prepare product state over L time slices; compute stock path sequentially in the log domain or price domain.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: No numerical hardware experiment reported; theoretical resource analysis only.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Lm + 1 for path registers plus ancilla; additional qubits may be needed for arithmetic registers
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: O(Lm) for preparing the product distribution state, plus reversible arithmetic for path averaging

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare L discretized Gaussian increment distributions and compute pathwise averages classically for benchmarking.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated expectation value to discounted option price.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming efficient preparation of L Gaussian increment states and efficient reversible arithmetic for path averaging
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical hardware experiment reported; result is a theoretical resource analysis only.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(lambda/epsilon) up to polylogarithmic factors for amplitude estimation-based pricing
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(lambda^2/epsilon^2) samples for classical Monte Carlo

experiments.description: Numerical comparison of quantum phase estimation versus classical Monte Carlo for a European call option, using a single-qubit phase-estimation surrogate to demonstrate quadratic error scaling.

algorithm.variant: Single-qubit phase estimation surrogate for amplitude estimation

hyperparameters.kQ: number of applications of the single-qubit unitary

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The analytical option price is converted to a phase theta and simulated via repeated applications of Uz = exp(-i theta sigma_z / 2).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the option price error scaling, Error = |Pi_hat - Pi|, as a function of Monte Carlo steps.

problem_instance.description: European call option benchmark with analytical Black-Scholes price used as ground truth.

dataset_specification.description: Same BSM parameters as the main European-call example; no external dataset.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Analytical price computed from Black-Scholes formula; rescaled to phase theta for the phase-estimation surrogate.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Log-log fit of error versus number of Monte Carlo steps; quantum and classical estimates matched to similar confidence (>99.5%).

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 1 logical qubit for the surrogate phase-estimation simulation; D independent runs used for confidence boosting
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Proportional to the number of unitary applications kQ; phase-estimation surrogate uses repeated powers of a single-qubit unitary

hardware.framework: single-qubit numerical simulation; no specific SDK named for this experiment

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute analytical Black-Scholes price and classical Monte Carlo baseline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Fit error scaling exponent; compare quantum and classical slopes; compute upper-bound error curve epsilon_Q.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Reported fitted quantum scaling exponent zeta_Q = -0.982 versus classical zeta_C = -0.5

speedup_claims.conditions: log-log fit of error versus Monte Carlo steps for a European call option benchmark; D ≈ 24 independent runs; similar confidence >99.5%
speedup_claims.caveats: The quantum result is from a single-qubit phase-estimation surrogate, not a full multi-qubit implementation.

speedup_claims.conditions: upper-bound error curve epsilon_Q scales with exponent -1
speedup_claims.caveats: Upper bound is derived from phase-estimation theory rather than direct hardware execution.

scalability_data.problem_size: number of Monte Carlo steps kQ

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Approximately O(1/epsilon) in the phase-estimation surrogate; more generally O(lambda/epsilon) up to polylog factors
